findings.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on default installs because the embed_category site setting row is typically absent, so the query returns zero rows and [0]['id'] calls nil['id']
Migration join s.value = c.name assumes the setting stores a category name, but it may store a category id, so the lookup silently falls through to uncategorized and topics land in the wrong category

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb was replaced with the embeddable_host fabricator, so the :category fabricator no longer lives in its convention-required filename and nearly every spec calling Fabricate(:category) will fail
Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when the embed_category site setting is empty, aborting the migration on fresh installs that never set embed_category

update with a nonexistent id calls nil.host = ... causing a 500 crash in embeddable_hosts_controller
destroy with a nonexistent id calls host.destroy on nil causing a 500

No spec verifies non-staff authorization rejection (ensure_staff) for the new controllers

expandable_first_post? behavior changed so it's true whenever embed_truncate? and has_topic_embed? hold regardless of host configuration; the existing spec passes for the wrong reason and no spec documents the new intended semantics

_hydrateEmbedded can produce arrays of nulls ([null, null]) instead of [] when subType lookup fails for ids, breaking {{#each}} rendering with no test coverage
Feed-polling path (Jobs::PollFeed/TopicRetriever) now gives category: nil for hosts not in embeddable_hosts, silently posting feeds to Uncategorized with no spec update

Admin embedding template only contains the hosts table and drops all other embedding settings (embed_by_username, feed_polling_*, embed_truncate, embed_post_limit, whitelist/blacklist selectors), leaving them with no admin UI surface

Fabricator files were swapped: category fabricators now live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and the embeddable_host fabricator lives in category_fabricator.rb, making dozens of specs depend on misnamed files
Admin EmbeddingController#update is a dead endpoint: it renders the serializer but never applies params, silently succeeding without persisting anything

Migration crashes with NoMethodError on installs where the embed_category site setting row does not exist, since [0] is nil before the fallback check
Destructive non-reversible deletion of embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no down path, and raw string interpolation without sanitization can break the INSERT

Empty host table no longer rejects with 'embeddable hosts not set' — it collapses into the same 'invalid referer host' error, and the invariant that embedding is disabled when unconfigured is untested and unenforced

The `update` action in admin/embedding_controller.rb is a no-op — it re-serializes @embedding without applying any params, so the advertised PUT route persists nothing and the admin UI silently discards input

Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb inserts old setting values verbatim via raw INSERT, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so migrated hosts like `https://example.com/1234` never match the lookup `lower(host) = URI(input).host`, silently breaking embedding for configured sites

Port drift between validation and lookup in embeddable_host.rb: the format regex accepts a port so `example.com:8080` can be stored, but `record_for_host` extracts `uri.host` which strips the port, so a host saved with a port can never match its own referer

Missing schema invariants in the embeddable_hosts migration: no UNIQUE constraint on `host` (allowing duplicate rows making category selection nondeterministic) and no index backing the per-request `lower(host) = ?` lookup, which is non-sargable anyway

Unguarded nil dereference in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update and destroy actions: `where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil, causing NoMethodError (500) instead of a 404 when acting on a stale/deleted record

Update path in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb trusts params[:embeddable_host][:host] unnormalized, relying solely on the model callback which never handles uppercase input (e.g. `EXAMPLE.COM` is stored as-is), creating a split-normalization drift surface between write-side stripping and read-side `lower()`

Client-side duplicated derived data in embeddable-host.js.es6: after save the component manually fabricates the category association via `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`, so when categoryId is blank the server silently saves to uncategorized while the client renders `undefined`, causing displayed state to drift from persisted state

Migration crashes on fresh installs because execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError when the embed_category setting row doesn't exist, aborting db:migrate for new sites
Migration interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts setting value into SQL INSERT without escaping, causing breakage or SQL injection if the value contains a quote

topic.rb expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard so any topic with a topic embed is expandable regardless of embedding configuration, and the spec change papers over this by no longer testing what its name claims

store.js.es6 plural branch never falls back to [] because hydrated (.map result) is always truthy, allowing [false, false] values and rendering a table with falsy rows instead of hiding the empty state

category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, silently rewiring where core fabricators are defined with no connection to the feature
embedding_controller update action is a no-op save path that re-renders the serializer without reading or persisting anything, while the frontend presents it as a functioning save
SQL string interpolation of unescaped values into raw INSERT in migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb, allowing malformed or injected SQL during migration
Host-allowlist check gates purely on client-supplied Referer header, which is a weak authorization basis

Normalization mismatch: stored hosts keep their port (before_validation strips only scheme and path) while record_for_host compares against port-stripped uri.host, so a host like example.com:8080 can never match, silently disabling the allowlist entry

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7 — the entire spec is a single class-inheritance assertion (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController) that passes no matter how broken the controller logic is; never issues a request, never checks authorization, save_host's error branch (render_json_error) or the category_id.blank? → uncategorized fallback

test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6:109 — find('fruit', 2) intends to hit a different fruit, but the pretender handler hardcodes fruits[0], so fruit 1 is fetched again; the single-element _ids path (color_ids: [3] / 'Yellow') has zero coverage, and the test mirrors fixtures so closely it would pass even if hydration returned raw ID arrays instead of hydrated records

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192-207 — the rewrite of _hydrateEmbedded silently changes key-deletion semantics: singular branch deletes category_id only when hydrated is truthy, plural branch sets hydrated || [] before deleting; failed singular lookups leaving the raw _id key behind, pluralize mapping, and the || [] fallback are all untested

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:12-15 — 'raises an error with a missing host' no longer sets anything and relies on no EmbeddableHost rows existing, making it indistinguishable from the 'no referer' test; the distinct failure surface (host_allowed? false with non-empty table and nil referer causing URI parse failure in record_for_host) is only exercised accidentally

cmd_tuples is always 0 for SELECTs in PostgreSQL, so the backfill never runs while the unconditional DELETE destroys the source site_settings data
Unguarded [0] on the embed_category lookup raises NoMethodError on fresh installs or sites without embed_category set, failing db:migrate/db:setup
create_table uses force: true, silently dropping the existing embeddable_hosts table and its rows if the migration is re-run after a partial run
Backfill inserts raw host strings without the model's normalization (stripping scheme/path), so migrated rows never match at read time and embeds 403
Migration deletes source-of-truth site_settings rows with no backup and no down method, making db:rollback permanently lose all embed configuration
embed_category is resolved by category name join, so renamed or recased categories silently fall back to uncategorized, misclassifying embedded topics
category_id has no foreign key and no cleanup on category deletion, leaving stale/orphaned category_id references that render blank category badges and nil categories on PostCreator
delete action in embeddable-host.js.es6 calls destroyRecord() with no .catch, so a failed DELETE gives no popupAjaxError and no user feedback
saveChanges() in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls embedding.update({}) with no .then/.catch, and the controller update action reads no params — a silent no-op reported as success
EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can return nil in update/destroy, causing NoMethodError and a raw 500 instead of 404/4xx for stale IDs
EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false on malformed URLs, and caller uses .try(:category_id) which doesn't short-circuit on false, crashing TopicEmbed.import
store.js.es6 plural hydration has no null guard and _lookupSubType returning false yields [false, false] since the || [] fallback can't fire for a non-empty truthy array, causing downstream crashes
save action optimistically sets host category via findById(categoryId) which may return undefined, letting the displayed badge and persisted model diverge silently

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration join s.value = c.name assumes the setting stores a category name, but it may store a category id, so the lookup silently falls through to uncategorized and topics land in the wrong category

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the initial `category_id` lookup does `INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`, i.e. it assumes `site_settings.value` equals `categories.name`. If `embed_category` was stored as a category id (or slug) rather than the name, this query will return no rows and the migration will silently fall back to `uncategorized_category_id`, causing migrated embeddable hosts (and thus embeds) to end up in the wrong category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy don't nil-check the fetched record, so stale or nonexistent ids cause a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404
EmbeddingController update never applies params or saves anything, making the save button a no-op request that always reports success with no data persisted

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action simply re-renders the current `@embedding` OpenStruct (`render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`) and never reads `params` or persists any changes. On the client, `admin-embedding.js.es6` defines a `saveChanges` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit that PUT endpoint but have no effect. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not show a save button wired to `saveChanges`, so the claim about a user-visible save button being a no-op isn’t directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration SQL-interpolates raw setting values into the INSERT, so quotes or backslashes in embeddable_hosts lines cause a SQL syntax error mid-migration, leaving it partially applied

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes from the old `site_settings` value split by lines. If any line contains a single-quote or backslash, it can break SQL parsing and cause the migration to error. The “partially applied” part depends on DB/transaction behavior, but the unescaped interpolation is a real, diff-grounded correctness risk that can make the migration fail on valid stored data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb was replaced with the embeddable_host fabricator, so the :category fabricator no longer lives in its convention-required filename and nearly every spec calling Fabricate(:category) will fail
Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when the embed_category site setting is empty, aborting the migration on fresh installs that never set embed_category

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` to derive `category_id` from the `embed_category` setting. If the JOIN returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` is empty/default or never set), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration before the `category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration compares raw serialized YAML value (s.value = c.name) against category names so the JOIN never matches and the fallback path is unreachable

adjudication.rationale: In the migration, the JOIN is `INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. Nothing in the diff shows `site_settings.value` is “raw serialized YAML”; it’s queried as a plain column value. Also, the fallback (`if category_id == 0 ...`) is present and conceptually reachable if the query returns an id of 0. While the migration may still be fragile (it does `[0]['id']` without handling an empty result), the specific claim that the JOIN “never matches” due to YAML and that the fallback is unreachable is not verifiable from this diff and misreads what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test exists for the data migration to embeddable_hosts

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a nontrivial data migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb (reads from site_settings, inserts rows into embeddable_hosts, then deletes old settings), but the added specs only cover controllers/models and there is no spec exercising or validating this migration behavior. The finding is therefore accurate and is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that only re-reads and re-renders without applying any params, while the frontend saveChanges sends an empty body, making the editable settings screen a documented no-op

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading/applying any params (new file `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`). The frontend controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` (new file `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`), i.e., an empty payload. However, the new `embedding.hbs` template does not call `saveChanges` at all (it only adds/saves/deletes individual `embeddable-host` records), so this no-op PUT path is currently unused rather than a directly user-visible broken screen. It’s still a concrete, diff-grounded concern: a dead/incomplete update endpoint + unused action that suggests intended editable settings aren’t actually persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb silently posts to Uncategorized (category: nil) when the embed URL's host is not an embeddable host, dropping the old SiteSetting.embed_category fallback with no spec covering the non-allowlisted host path

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, the category assignment changed from `category: SiteSetting.embed_category` to `category: eh.try(:category_id)` after `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`. If no `EmbeddableHost` matches, `eh` is `nil` and `category` becomes `nil`, with no in-method guard to prevent topic creation in that case. The diff also removes the `embed_category` setting entirely (`config/site_settings.yml` and `server.en.yml`). Specs only cover the allowlisted case (e.g., `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` asserts the category equals `embeddable_host.category`) and do not cover the non-allowlisted path. However, the claim that it "silently posts to Uncategorized" is not directly verifiable from this diff because `PostCreator`'s behavior for `category: nil` is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs only assert class inheritance and never verify create/update/destroy behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new controller specs `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`, and both only test that the controller is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. They do not exercise or assert behavior of the newly added actions in the controllers (e.g., `create/update/destroy` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `show/update` in `Admin::EmbeddingController`), so CRUD/behavioral coverage for these new endpoints is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update with a nonexistent id calls nil.host = ... causing a 500 crash in embeddable_hosts_controller

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the record is fetched with `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally passed to `save_host(host)`. If no record exists, `host` is `nil` and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...`, causing a `NoMethodError` (500). (Similarly, `destroy` calls `host.destroy` without a nil-check.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroy with a nonexistent id calls host.destroy on nil causing a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy`. If no record exists for the given `id`, `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise, causing a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The blank-category fallback (host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if blank) is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code explicitly falls back when the client supplies a blank category (`host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`). The added specs do not cover this behavior: `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only checks inheritance, and `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` only tests host trimming and `host_allowed?`, not category fallback. So this is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test issue for newly added logic, not a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec verifies non-staff authorization rejection (ensure_staff) for the new controllers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new admin controllers with access control filters (`before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` in `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` and `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`). The accompanying specs (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) only assert the controllers subclass `Admin::AdminController` and do not exercise/verify that non-staff users are rejected by `ensure_staff` (or even that requests are blocked). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test gap for newly added authorization logic, but not a defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? behavior changed so it's true whenever embed_truncate? and has_topic_embed? hold regardless of host configuration; the existing spec passes for the wrong reason and no spec documents the new intended semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic.rb`, `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing any dependency on allowed-host configuration. In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer sets any host-related state but still expects `false`; it will pass because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to false and/or `has_topic_embed?` isn’t stubbed, not because hosts are blank. Likewise the `describe 'with an emeddable host'` block fabricates an `EmbeddableHost`, but the method under test never consults it, so those tests don't actually assert the new semantics. This is a real, diff-grounded test/intent clarity issue rather than a provable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No frontend/JS tests exist for the new admin embedding UI, including save action category_id mapping, cancel behavior, and adapter pathFor

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new admin embedding UI and client-side logic (e.g., `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` with `pathFor() { return "/admin/customize/embedding"; }`, `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` actions `save/cancel/delete` including `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`, and the `admin-embedding` route/controller/templates). However, the only JS tests changed/added in this PR are store hydration tests (`test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6`) and pretender fixtures (`create-pretender.js.es6`); there are no frontend tests covering the new embedding UI behaviors like category_id mapping on save, cancel behavior for new vs existing hosts, or the adapter path. This is a concrete missing-test gap for newly introduced nontrivial UI logic, but not itself a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adapter pathFor returns '/admin/customize/embedding' which may not align with the resources :embeddable_hosts REST route expectations

adjudication.rationale: The new `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` adapter is for the `embedding` model and its `pathFor()` returns `/admin/customize/embedding`, which matches the added Rails routes (`get`/`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#show/update"`). The `resources :embeddable_hosts` REST endpoints are separate and are supported by updating `RestAdapter`’s `ADMIN_MODELS` to include `'embeddable-host'`, causing that model to use the `/admin/embeddable_hosts` base path. There is no demonstrated misalignment between the embedding adapter path and the embeddable_hosts resource routes in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded can produce arrays of nulls ([null, null]) instead of [] when subType lookup fails for ids, breaking {{#each}} rendering with no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, the new plural hydration path (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/`) does `obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and assigns the result directly to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`. If `_lookupSubType` returns `null/undefined` for an id (e.g., ids present but the embedded records are missing from `root`), this will produce arrays like `[null, null]` rather than `[]` or a filtered list. The `|| []` guard does not help because an array is always truthy. Existing tests only cover the success case where `colors` are included, so the failure/edge case isn’t covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed-polling path (Jobs::PollFeed/TopicRetriever) now gives category: nil for hosts not in embeddable_hosts, silently posting feeds to Uncategorized with no spec update

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes host validation to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`), which would *block* embed/feed processing when the host is not in the allowed-host table, rather than “silently posting” anything. While `TopicEmbed.import` now sets `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (so category could be `nil` if no matching `EmbeddableHost` is found), the claim specifically ties this to “hosts not in embeddable_hosts” and “silently posting feeds to Uncategorized,” which is not supported by any shown logic in this diff (no posting path shown, and the host-not-allowed path now raises/invalidates earlier).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embedding template only contains the hosts table and drops all other embedding settings (embed_by_username, feed_polling_*, embed_truncate, embed_post_limit, whitelist/blacklist selectors), leaving them with no admin UI surface

adjudication.rationale: The new admin embedding template (app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs) indeed only renders the embeddable hosts table, but the diff does not remove the other embedding settings from the admin UI surface: they remain defined in config/site_settings.yml under the `embedding:` section (feed_polling_enabled/url, embed_by_username, embed_username_key_from_feed, embed_post_limit, embed_truncate, whitelist/blacklist selectors). Only `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` are removed from site settings and replaced by the new EmbeddableHost model/UI. Therefore the claim that the remaining settings have “no admin UI surface” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files were swapped: category fabricators now live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and the embeddable_host fabricator lives in category_fabricator.rb, making dozens of specs depend on misnamed files
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about swapped contents causing loss/misuse/errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddingController#update is a dead endpoint: it renders the serializer but never applies params, silently succeeding without persisting anything

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op: it just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads/applies `params` (and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`, not a persisted model), so a PUT will always “succeed” without changing anything. However, the new admin UI template (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) doesn’t expose a save action (it only adds/edits/deletes `EmbeddableHost` records via the separate `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`), so this is more of an unnecessary/dead endpoint/API semantics issue than a demonstrated broken user flow in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store.js hydration semantic change: singular branch now only deletes obj[k] when hydration succeeds, causing stray _id attributes to remain in JSON payloads for unrelated models when subtype lookup fails

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` the pre-existing singular `_id` hydration branch already only did `delete obj[k]` when `hydrated` was truthy (`if (hydrated) { obj[subType] = hydrated; delete obj[k]; }`). The new code preserves that exact behavior for the singular case. The only semantic change shown is adding plural `_ids` handling, where it *always* deletes `obj[k]` after mapping, not less. So the claimed “semantic change” causing stray `_id` attributes is not introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on installs where the embed_category site setting row does not exist, since [0] is nil before the fallback check
Destructive non-reversible deletion of embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no down path, and raw string interpolation without sanitization can break the INSERT

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If a stored host value contains a single-quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the migration can fail or produce incorrect SQL; this is unsanitized input coming from `site_settings.value`. The same migration also permanently deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` settings (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`) inside a `change` method with raw `execute`, making rollback non-reversible and causing data loss on rollback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Empty host table no longer rejects with 'embeddable hosts not set' — it collapses into the same 'invalid referer host' error, and the invariant that embedding is disabled when unconfigured is untested and unenforced

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit “unconfigured” guard in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`: the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` check and its `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set')` raise are deleted, leaving only `raise ... 'invalid referer host' unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). With an empty `embeddable_hosts` table, `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` returns false, so the request is still rejected, but the error collapses into the same 'invalid referer host' case. Tests were updated to no longer set `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil` and instead rely on the absence/presence of fabricated `EmbeddableHost` records, without asserting a distinct “embedding disabled/unconfigured” condition (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/contract change and potential missing coverage, but not a verifiable functional defect since access is still denied when unconfigured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `update` action in admin/embedding_controller.rb is a no-op — it re-serializes @embedding without applying any params, so the advertised PUT route persists nothing and the admin UI silently discards input

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `def update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads/applies `params`, so the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` endpoint is effectively a no-op. However, the diff’s UI mainly persists changes via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save` / `destroyRecord`), and the only client call shown is `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }` (empty payload, and there’s no save button in `embedding.hbs`). So this is dead/placeholder behavior rather than a verified “silently discards input” defect in the current UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb inserts old setting values verbatim via raw INSERT, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so migrated hosts like `https://example.com/1234` never match the lookup `lower(host) = URI(input).host`, silently breaking embedding for configured sites

Port drift between validation and lookup in embeddable_host.rb: the format regex accepts a port so `example.com:8080` can be stored, but `record_for_host` extracts `uri.host` which strips the port, so a host saved with a port can never match its own referer

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `validates_format_of :host` regex explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` normalization strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, so values like `example.com:8080` can be persisted. However, `record_for_host` parses the referer with `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which returns only the hostname without the port, and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means a stored record containing a port (e.g. `example.com:8080`) will never match a referer from the same origin (`http://example.com:8080/...`), causing `host_allowed?` to incorrectly return false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing schema invariants in the embeddable_hosts migration: no UNIQUE constraint on `host` (allowing duplicate rows making category selection nondeterministic) and no index backing the per-request `lower(host) = ?` lookup, which is non-sargable anyway

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with only `host` and `category_id` (no unique constraint or index). The model lookup used for request-time authorization/category resolution is `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` → `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so duplicate `host` rows are allowed (no DB constraint and no `validates_uniqueness_of`), and `first` makes the selected row/category effectively nondeterministic. Additionally, there’s no index to support the frequent `lower(host)` lookup, creating a real performance issue for per-request checks (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded nil dereference in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update and destroy actions: `where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil, causing NoMethodError (500) instead of a 404 when acting on a stale/deleted record

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately uses `host` (`save_host(host)` which assigns `host.host = ...`, and `host.destroy`). If the record doesn't exist (stale/deleted id), `host` will be `nil`, leading to a `NoMethodError` (500) rather than a controlled 404/invalid response. There is no nil guard shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb trusts params[:embeddable_host][:host] unnormalized, relying solely on the model callback which never handles uppercase input (e.g. `EXAMPLE.COM` is stored as-is), creating a split-normalization drift surface between write-side stripping and read-side `lower()`
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to a case-normalization mismatch: the lookup uses a case-insensitive comparison via lower(host), but inputs/parameters (referer host or stored host) are not consistently normalized to lowercase, so mixed-case hosts (e.g., EXAMPLE.COM) can fail to match. The candidate frames it as write-side vs read-side drift, which is the same underlying bug as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side duplicated derived data in embeddable-host.js.es6: after save the component manually fabricates the category association via `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`, so when categoryId is blank the server silently saves to uncategorized while the client renders `undefined`, causing displayed state to drift from persisted state

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `save()` sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` but `cantSave` only validates `buffered.host`, not `categoryId`, so `categoryId` can be `null`/blank for a new host. On the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` coerces blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. After a successful save, the client manually sets `host.category` via `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`; if `categoryId` was blank this sets `category` to `undefined`, causing the UI to drift from persisted state (server saved uncategorized).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs because execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError when the embed_category setting row doesn't exist, aborting db:migrate for new sites

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If that query returns zero rows (e.g., fresh install with no `site_settings` row for `embed_category`), `[...] [0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting `db:migrate` before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts setting value into SQL INSERT without escaping, causing breakage or SQL injection if the value contains a quote

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes directly from the stored `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` split by newlines. If any host line contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), this will at least break the migration and could allow SQL injection within the migration execution context. The diff shows no escaping/quoting (e.g., connection.quote) is applied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.rb expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard so any topic with a topic embed is expandable regardless of embedding configuration, and the spec change papers over this by no longer testing what its name claims

adjudication.rationale: The diff does drop the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` condition in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (now only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`), but the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting was removed/migrated to the `EmbeddableHost` model, so it’s not clearly a defect that the guard disappeared. However, the updated spec is misleading/weak: `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer sets `embed_truncate` true nor stubs `has_topic_embed?` true, so it doesn’t actually test the scenario its name implies, and fabricating an `:embeddable_host` in the “with an embeddable host” context doesn’t affect the method under test (which no longer checks host configuration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6 plural branch never falls back to [] because hydrated (.map result) is always truthy, allowing [false, false] values and rendering a table with falsy rows instead of hiding the empty state

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` plural hydration (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`), `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` always returns an Array (truthy), so `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` never falls back to `[]`. If `_lookupSubType` can return a falsy value for an unknown/missing id (analogous to the singular branch which checks `if (hydrated)` before assigning), the resulting relationship array can contain falsy entries (e.g., `[false, false]`) instead of being empty/omitted, which can lead to iterating/rendering over invalid rows downstream.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, silently rewiring where core fabricators are defined with no connection to the feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was rewritten to define only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (and no longer defines any category-related fabricators), while the prior category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into a new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/organization issue: fabricators are now defined in files whose names no longer match their contents, and core category fabricators were relocated as part of an embedding feature change. It’s not clearly a functional defect from the diff alone (Fabrication typically loads all files under `spec/fabricators` regardless of filename), but it is a confusing refactor with weak connection to the feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embedding_controller update action is a no-op save path that re-renders the serializer without reading or persisting anything, while the frontend presents it as a functioning save

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` without applying params or persisting anything (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `def update ... render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`). On the client, there is an `admin-embedding` controller action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`), implying an updatable resource. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not actually wire up a save button/action, and host changes are persisted via `EmbeddableHost` create/update/destroy instead, so the “frontend presents it as a functioning save” part isn’t verifiable from this diff alone. Still, having an exposed PUT route with a no-op update path is a concrete, diff-grounded design/incompleteness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL string interpolation of unescaped values into raw INSERT in migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb, allowing malformed or injected SQL during migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes from splitting the existing `site_settings` value and is not escaped/quoted safely, so a host containing `'` (or worse, crafted SQL) could break the migration or inject SQL during migration execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host-allowlist check gates purely on client-supplied Referer header, which is a weak authorization basis

adjudication.rationale: The embed access control in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer` for authorization: `raise ... unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (changed in this diff from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)`). Since `Referer` is a client-supplied header that can be spoofed/omitted, this is a weak basis for enforcing an allowlist and is a security defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Normalization mismatch: stored hosts keep their port (before_validation strips only scheme and path) while record_for_host compares against port-stripped uri.host, so a host like example.com:8080 can never match, silently disabling the allowlist entry

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost` the `before_validation` normalization strips only scheme and path (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//,'')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/,'')`), so an input like `example.com:8080` is stored with the port intact. But `record_for_host` parses the referer/url via `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`; `uri.host` excludes the port (it would be `example.com`). Therefore a stored allowlist entry containing a port (which is explicitly allowed by the model validation regex) will never match and will incorrectly deny embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7 — the entire spec is a single class-inheritance assertion (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController) that passes no matter how broken the controller logic is; never issues a request, never checks authorization, save_host's error branch (render_json_error) or the category_id.blank? → uncategorized fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` with only an inheritance assertion (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`). This test will pass even if `create/update/destroy` or `save_host` are broken, and it does not exercise authorization (`before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`), the error path (`render_json_error(host)`), or the `category_id.blank?` fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` in `save_host`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than an application defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7 — same pattern: only assertion is the subclass check, no request is ever made; notably the controller's update action doesn't call update on anything (arguably a source bug) and nothing in the spec would catch it

adjudication.rationale: The new `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only asserts `Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController` and never exercises `GET #show` or `PUT #update`, so it provides no coverage for the controller’s behavior. This is especially relevant because `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` in the diff simply re-renders `@embedding` without applying any params or persisting anything, and the current spec would not detect if that endpoint is unintentionally a no-op or regresses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6:109 — find('fruit', 2) intends to hit a different fruit, but the pretender handler hardcodes fruits[0], so fruit 1 is fetched again; the single-element _ids path (color_ids: [3] / 'Yellow') has zero coverage, and the test mirrors fixtures so closely it would pass even if hydration returned raw ID arrays instead of hydrated records

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the Pretender route for `GET /fruits/:id` hardcodes `const fruit = fruits[0];` regardless of the requested `:id` (test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6). Meanwhile, the updated test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts it has two hydrated `colors` with ids 1 and 2 (test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6), which matches fruit id 1’s fixture (`color_ids: [1,2]`), not fruit id 2’s fixture (`color_ids: [3]`). So the test is not actually exercising the `:id` lookup nor the single-element `*_ids` hydration path; it can pass even if the handler ignores the id. This is a concrete test/fixture issue (coverage/validity), not a production behavior defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192-207 — the rewrite of _hydrateEmbedded silently changes key-deletion semantics: singular branch deletes category_id only when hydrated is truthy, plural branch sets hydrated || [] before deleting; failed singular lookups leaving the raw _id key behind, pluralize mapping, and the || [] fallback are all untested

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6 the singular *_id branch still only deletes obj[k] when `hydrated` is truthy, exactly as in the pre-change code; this is not a “rewrite” semantic change. The new plural *_ids handling (mapping `color_ids` -> `colors` and deleting the raw key) is also explicitly exercised by the updated JS tests (store-test.js.es6) and pretender fixtures (create-pretender.js.es6). While edge cases (e.g., failed lookups yielding undefined entries) aren’t covered, the finding’s claims that these behaviors are “silently changed” and “all untested” don’t match the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1400-1404 — test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' is stale/mislabeled since the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? check was removed from expandable_first_post?; the test passes only for unrelated reasons (embed_truncate defaults false, has_topic_embed? unstubbed), and no test covers that a topic with no hosts but embed_truncate=true and a topic_embed would now return true

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard from `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (topic.rb: `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In the updated spec, the test still says "is false if embeddable_host is blank" but no longer sets any host-related state, and it would return false simply because `embed_truncate` is not enabled and `has_topic_embed?` is not stubbed in that example. So the finding that the test is stale/mislabeled and not actually asserting host-related behavior is verifiable from the diff; it's a test-quality/coverage issue rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:12-15 — 'raises an error with a missing host' no longer sets anything and relies on no EmbeddableHost rows existing, making it indistinguishable from the 'no referer' test; the distinct failure surface (host_allowed? false with non-empty table and nil referer causing URI parse failure in record_for_host) is only exercised accidentally

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the "raises an error with a missing host" test no longer sets `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil` (removed in the diff) and does not create any `EmbeddableHost` records. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb — the model spec tests only valid inputs; the validation-failure branch (invalid host format), before_validation mutation interacting with validation (sub! on nil host would raise), and destructive self.host.sub! on existing records are all untested, so the admin-typo error path has no spec
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that the before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` and will raise `NoMethodError` when `self.host` is nil. The candidate explicitly mentions the same problem (“sub! on nil host would raise”) in the context of untested validation/mutation behavior, so it identifies the same underlying bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cmd_tuples is always 0 for SELECTs in PostgreSQL, so the backfill never runs while the unconditional DELETE destroys the source site_settings data

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the backfill gate uses `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` after `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")`. For PostgreSQL, `cmd_tuples` is based on `PQcmdTuples` and is not reliable for `SELECT` (often yields 0/empty), so this condition can prevent the backfill from running even when a row exists. The migration then unconditionally executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, which would drop the source data without having copied it into `embeddable_hosts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded [0] on the embed_category lookup raises NoMethodError on fresh installs or sites without embed_category set, failing db:migrate/db:setup

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` to look up the category for the `embed_category` site setting. If that query returns no rows (fresh install or `embed_category` not set), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` will raise `NoMethodError` before the subsequent `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table uses force: true, silently dropping the existing embeddable_hosts table and its rows if the migration is re-run after a partial run

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the table with `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which would delete any existing `embeddable_hosts` rows if the migration is re-run (e.g., after a partial/failed run or in certain reset/reapply workflows).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill inserts raw host strings without the model's normalization (stripping scheme/path), so migrated rows never match at read time and embeds 403
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the backfill uses raw SQL/strings and bypasses the model’s normalization (stripping scheme/path), causing migrated hosts not to match lookups at read time. This is the same core issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration deletes source-of-truth site_settings rows with no backup and no down method, making db:rollback permanently lose all embed configuration

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` copies existing `site_settings` values into the new `embeddable_hosts` table, then executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. There is no `down`/reversible logic to restore those rows (and `execute` statements inside `change` make rollback non-reversible), so a rollback (or forced rollback) would not be able to recover the prior settings. However, it’s not strictly “no backup” during the forward migration because values are migrated into `embeddable_hosts`; the issue is irreversibility/rollback safety rather than immediate data loss in the normal upgrade path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_category is resolved by category name join, so renamed or recased categories silently fall back to uncategorized, misclassifying embedded topics

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` resolves the old `embed_category` setting by joining `site_settings.value` to `categories.name` (`INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`). If the category name no longer exactly matches the stored setting value (e.g., renamed/recased), the query yields no rows, `category_id` becomes 0, and the code falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`, silently migrating embeddable hosts to the wrong category and thus misclassifying subsequently imported embedded topics (since `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_id has no foreign key and no cleanup on category deletion, leaving stale/orphaned category_id references that render blank category badges and nil categories on PostCreator

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `embeddable_hosts.category_id` (migration creates an integer column `null: false`, model `belongs_to :category`) but does not add a DB foreign key or any explicit handling when a `Category` is deleted. This makes orphaned `category_id` values possible, which would yield `host.category == nil` (e.g., the admin UI renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`). However, the diff alone doesn’t prove categories can be deleted in a way that causes observable breakage in `PostCreator` (behavior not shown here), so it’s best treated as a concrete integrity/edge-case concern rather than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: delete action in embeddable-host.js.es6 calls destroyRecord() with no .catch, so a failed DELETE gives no popupAjaxError and no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but has no `.catch(...)` handler. Since `popupAjaxError` is imported (and used for `save()`), a failed DELETE request would provide no user-facing error feedback (and potentially trigger an unhandled promise rejection), which is a real behavioral defect grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: saveChanges() in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls embedding.update({}) with no .then/.catch, and the controller update action reads no params — a silent no-op reported as success

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});` with an empty hash and no `.then/.catch` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6). On the server, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the serializer and does not read or apply any params (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb), making the PUT effectively a no-op. However, the UI template added (admin/templates/embedding.hbs) doesn’t include any save button or invoke `saveChanges`; host changes are persisted via `host.save(props)` in the `embeddable-host` component. So it’s a real, diff-grounded concern (misleading/dead endpoint/action and lack of error handling) but not a demonstrated broken behavior in the shown flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can return nil in update/destroy, causing NoMethodError and a raw 500 instead of 404/4xx for stale IDs
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first may return nil in update/destroy and that calling methods on it would raise a NoMethodError (leading to a 500 instead of handling missing record). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment: lack of validation/handling when the record isn’t found.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false on malformed URLs, and caller uses .try(:category_id) which doesn't short-circuit on false, crashing TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` may return `false` on malformed/unknown URLs, but `eh.try(:category_id)` will not crash: ActiveSupport `try` returns `nil` when the receiver does not respond to the method (and `false` does not respond to `category_id`). The diff shows no `.category_id` call without `try`, so the claimed crash is not supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6 plural hydration has no null guard and _lookupSubType returning false yields [false, false] since the || [] fallback can't fire for a non-empty truthy array, causing downstream crashes

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` plural hydration was added: `const hydrated = obj[k].map(..._lookupSubType...)` then `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy), the `|| []` fallback will never run, and if `_lookupSubType` returns `false` for missing IDs the resulting relation becomes e.g. `[false, false]`. Also there is no guard if `obj[k]` is `null/undefined`, so calling `.map` would throw. This is directly introduced by the diff’s new plural branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save action optimistically sets host category via findById(categoryId) which may return undefined, letting the displayed badge and persisted model diverge silently

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, after a successful save the code does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));`. The diff does not guarantee that `Discourse.Category` has that category loaded/available on the client (the embedding payload embeds `embeddable_hosts` but does not include category objects), so `findById` can plausibly return `undefined/null`, leaving `host.category` unset while `category_id` was persisted. That would cause the UI (`{{category-badge host.category}}`) to show nothing or behave inconsistently, but it’s an edge-case/data-availability concern rather than a definitively broken path shown by the diff.
